final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is relevant, but it does not cure the core audit defect: the available evidence still does not show compliance with the internal release-policy predicate requiring disclosure or approved risk acceptance for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case. This is why the case remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats. A caveated compliant outcome would require evidence that the caveat had been operationalized in a policy-satisfying way, such as actual disclosure or approved risk acceptance. Here, the caveat identifies an unresolved compliance condition instead of resolving it. Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring provide some support for launch-readiness direction, but not enough to establish policy compliance on the present record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the material limitation for the named launch use case was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved 1.3-point gap.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, leaving a policy predicate unresolved.
The affected fraud dispute review segment is named in two bank pilot commitments, so product's non-core characterization does not resolve materiality under the policy.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring, but they do not satisfy the internal disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
